why: Built slice B1 of docs/plan/quests/sev-runbooks-PLAN.md in today's lead tooling (0611): Route.admin with sev0, sev0Fixes and sev1 and a fix case with the ancestor check in pr/Merge.ts and land.ts; the fix entry, sev1Fix and sev0Fixes in sev/scripts/Level.ts; Incident.fix, Incident.drop and a close that dispatches scheduled.yaml on main in sev/scripts/Incident.ts; WorkflowRuns.dispatch in the contract, the gh layer and the test layer; main's check push run kept in Freeze.ts; sev.ts fix and fix --drop; the runbook case of Finding, Runbooks.ts and records check runbook in kalfa/records; the eight .runbooks/sev-*.md; the sev skill cut to its judgment and a list of the runbooks; and one sentence of the lead skill. Every law of the tests row is green, file by file, and all 30 of its plants went red on the real build.
note: Started and ended are estimates; usage and cost are not recorded. The container has Node 22, so the laws ran on the Node 26.13.0 the tests step fetched outside the repo. pnpm lint was green except lint:promise-types, which the kernel killed for memory once (EPIPE) and which passed alone. The whole pnpm typecheck was killed for memory once (SIGKILL on three packages) and passed with the same recursive command at one package at a time. A sev1's named fix is read from the issues its fix line answered, not from a clock: the sev tests run on a test clock that starts in 1970, so a time comparison against an issue's start would drop every named fix. Plant 0 is the plan's old verdict made on the real build by taking out the new case, not the old file.
